caption_used: The effect of context masking on case tasks grouped by language family, with error bars indicating standard deviation. Six model configurations are compared across nine language families: mBERT-L2, XLM-L2, mBERT-R2, XLM-R2, mBERT-B2, and XLM-B2. The IE-Indic family shows the largest effects overall, with most configurations reaching between 17 and 25, while Uralic and Isolate families show near-zero effects across all models. Notably, IE-Germanic exhibits consistently higher effects than IE-Romance across all configurations, with XLM-B2 reaching approximately 20 in IE-Germanic. The Semitic family displays the widest error bars overall, suggesting high variability, and the mBERT-L2 bars in Semitic reach approximately 15. In IE-Slavic, the B2 variants (mBERT-B2 and XLM-B2) dominate over the L2 and R2 variants, with effects approximately twice as large.
raw_response:
The grouped bar chart illustrates the effect of context masking on case tasks across different language families, comparing six model configurations. The horizontal axis, labeled "family," displays nine categories arranged alphabetically: IE-Baltic, IE-Germanic, IE-Indic, IE-Romance, IE-Slavic, IE-other, Isolate, Semitic, and Uralic. The vertical axis, labeled "effect," uses a linear scale with numeric tick marks and corresponding horizontal grid lines at intervals of 10, specifically at 0, 10, 20, and 30. Within each language family category, the data is represented by a group of six adjacent bars. A legend on the right side identifies the model configurations corresponding to each bar color: mBERT-L2 (light blue), XLM-L2 (dark blue), mBERT-R2 (light green), XLM-R2 (dark green), mBERT-B2 (light red), and XLM-B2 (dark red). Every bar features a black outline and a vertical black error bar with caps, indicating standard deviation. The bar heights vary across the categories; the shortest bars, representing near-zero effects, are found in the Isolate and Uralic families across all models. The tallest bars are located in the IE-Indic family, where the mBERT-B2 bar reaches approximately 24 and the mBERT-R2 bar reaches approximately 20. Other notable values include the mBERT-B2 and XLM-B2 bars in IE-Germanic and IE-Slavic, which range from approximately 15 to 17, and the XLM-L2 bar in Semitic, which reaches approximately 16 and displays a wide error bar extending up to nearly 30. A few bars, such as the R2 variants in IE-Germanic and Semitic, extend slightly below the zero line.
